evidence_type: direct assay; mutant phenotype; localization; interaction
claim_tested: A trans-spliced Gsdmd-Tmem106a chimera exists and modulates GSDMD pore assembly
key_finding: Chimeric mRNA joins Gsdmd exon 2 to Tmem106a exon 6; protein at plasma membrane; binds GSDMD-NT; accelerates pore formation and IL-1b release; stop knock-in and overexpression mice alter sepsis outcome
limitations: Discovery rests on 1 of 36826 chimeric reads; backed by targeted PCR/Sanger in 3 strains, MYC knock-in, stop knock-in, in vivo phenotypes. No human experiment on this pair.

claim_tested: GSDMD and TMEM106A are arranged so a read-through is possible
key_finding: Mouse chr15:75733974-75739257 (+) vs chr11:101473064-101482633 (+); human chr8:143553207-143563062 (+) vs chr17:43211835-43220041 (+). Different chromosomes in both species; intergenic distance undefined

claim_tested: A human chimera would preserve the caspase site and pore-forming domain
key_finding: It would not. Junction at GSDMD exon 2 (aa 1-73); caspase P1 Asp275 is the last codon of exon 7; GSDMD-NT is aa 1-275
limitations: Validated against 4 independent landmarks in the paper's mutant nomenclature and knock-in sequence.

citation: This work (Ensembl exon and genomic-region sequences)
claim_tested: The human locus is splice-competent for the same junction
key_finding: Identical phase-1 donor, GT donor and AG acceptor, identical 141-nt phase-0 exon 6, identical 44-codon +2 ORF stopping in exon 6, all tested residues conserved (F49/W50; E71/E73/D88/D91)
limitations: In silico only; predicts nothing about whether the event occurs.

claim_tested: The chimeric reading frame is under selection
key_finding: It is not. Observed alt-frame ORF 44 codons vs null median 5 (mouse) and 7 (human); p=0.117 and p=0.086. Alt-frame cross-species identity 55.6% vs 47.7% for the unused +1 control frame and 72.3% native
limitations: Uniform-synonym null may be conservative; codon-usage-weighted null could shift p modestly. Direction unambiguous.

citation: PMID:42686912 Suppl. Tables 11 and 12; Source Data Fig. 1b
claim_tested: Absence from the human dataset indicates a species difference
key_finding: It does not. 0/1441 human chimeric reads and 0/33 conserved pairs are GSDMD or TMEM106A, but the pipeline recovered conservation for only 33/30390 = 0.109% of mouse chimeras; 22/33 conserved pairs were single-read mouse singletons, as was Gsdmd-Tmem106a; per-read power 3.8%; one-sided binomial p=0.96
organism_context: Human monocyte-derived macrophages vs mouse BMDM
limitations: Computed directly from the authors' deposited source data.

citation: Ensembl; NCBI Gene; NCBI nuccore; UniProtKB (2026-11-25)
claim_tested: A human GSDMD-TMEM106A transcript is annotated somewhere
key_finding: All 28 Ensembl GRCh38 GSDMD transcripts confined to chr8:143553207-143563062; no NCBI readthrough locus; 0 nuccore records for GSDMD-TMEM106A; UniProt P57764 is a single 484-aa entry with 0 alternative products
limitations: ChimerDB 4.0 and ChiTaRS 5.0 have no documented REST API and could not be queried programmatically from this environment.

claim_tested: TMEM106A is present in human cells where GSDMD pores form
key_finding: TMEM106A is a type II transmembrane protein constitutively expressed in macrophages; raised by LPS and in peripheral monocytes of sepsis patients. Tmem106a-null mice are MORE sensitive to LPS septic shock, opposite to the chimera-null phenotype
limitations: Gene-level knockout removes native protein and chimera together; cannot adjudicate between them.

claim_tested: Parent transcripts are co-expressed in human myeloid cells
key_finding: TMEM106A immune cell enriched, 138.4 nCPM in macrophage/monocyte compartment; GSDMD detected in all blood cell types

claim_tested: The chimera is the accessory cofactor of GSDMD-NT pore assembly
key_finding: Genome-wide CRISPR screen in macrophages identifies Rabgef1 as a positive regulator: Rabgef1 deficiency preserves NT-GSDMD membrane binding but prevents NT-GSDMD oligomerization and lytic death, via plasma-membrane cholesterol
limitations: Offers a better-supported non-chimeric answer to the same mechanistic question.

claim_tested: Existing GO annotation covers a chimeric-cofactor route
key_finding: 87 annotations (14 MF, 20 BP, 23 CC). None mentions TMEM106A, chimera or trans-splicing. MF set is lipid binding, GO:0022829 wide pore channel activity (IDA, PMID:33883744), and one generic GO:0005515 (IPI, PMID:25416956)
